vectors.name: vintage-same-side-batch--winner-Y
vectors.note: exercises the block-vintage batching rule of the paper's section 4.4: same-vintage entries vest against the books as of vintage start (never to each other), capacity granted by a vintage becomes usable only from the next, and joint demand over a binding headroom is rationed pro-rata by offered size

vectors.name: r1-rationing-single-pass-n3--winner-A
vectors.note: section 4.4 (iii) is a SINGLE pass: joint demand D_w is the sum of OFFERED amounts, each entry's cap on w is floor(c*H_w/D_w), accepted = min over opposing books; headroom stranded on C by e1's cut on B (1924 units) is NOT re-offered. Expected accepted: e1 8076, e2 10000, e3 25000. A redistributing implementation returns e1 = 10000 and is non-conformant

vectors.name: p12-dust-seed-unbounded-kappa--winner-A
vectors.note: section 4.3 / 4.6: at unbounded kappa a 1-unit/leg seed passes P11 and a 10000-unit first entry is accepted in full; if B wins the 1-unit B leg collects all 10000 (the Appendix A.1 toll). The defence is the venue's MINIMUM SEED policy; this vector pins the mechanism's behaviour without one
